name: Resource Contention
essence: Independent actors each act in self-interest and exhaust a shared, finite resource.

examples.summary: One goroutine per user with no limit floods a 20-connection database.
examples.mechanism: Unbounded fan-out exceeds a finite shared pool (CWE-770).
examples.observed_output: queries rejected by connection limit: true
examples.expected_behavior: queries rejected by connection limit: false

examples.summary: Acquiring a slot blocks without a deadline, so a health check waits behind long reports.
examples.mechanism: Channel semaphore send has no context/timeout; callers starve.

examples.summary: A new `http.Transport` per call prevents connection reuse; every request opens a new socket.
examples.mechanism: Transports own the connection pool; creating one per request defeats pooling.

examples.summary: Request handlers send to an unbuffered channel drained by a slow consumer, so every request waits on it.
examples.mechanism: Unbuffered send blocks until the receiver is ready, coupling request latency to the auditor.

examples.summary: Spawning an OS thread per upload creates hundreds of threads.
examples.mechanism: Unbounded thread creation exhausts scheduler and memory (CWE-770).

examples.summary: An unbounded mpsc channel lets the producer queue thousands of events the consumer can't keep up with.
examples.mechanism: No backpressure: memory grows with the backlog. Use sync_channel.

examples.summary: The mutex guard is held across a slow fetch, serializing all workers.
examples.mechanism: Lock scope covers I/O; contention turns parallel work sequential (CWE-833).
examples.observed_output: 4 parallel refreshes ran one at a time: true
examples.expected_behavior: 4 parallel refreshes ran one at a time: false

examples.summary: All 100 requests are started at once against an API limited to 5 in flight.
examples.mechanism: Promise.all/allSettled over map starts everything immediately (CWE-770).

examples.summary: A synchronous hashing loop blocks the event loop, delaying every timer and request.
examples.mechanism: The single event-loop thread is a shared resource monopolized by CPU work.

examples.summary: Events are enqueued faster than drained with no bound, so memory grows without limit.
examples.mechanism: No backpressure or cap on a shared in-memory queue (CWE-400).

examples.summary: A failing query throws before `release()`, draining the pool so healthy queries wait forever.
examples.mechanism: Release not in finally; each error permanently removes a connection (CWE-772).
examples.observed_output: healthy query still waiting for a connection after 200ms

examples.summary: Eight items start eight threads, and the peak in the critical section is 8.
examples.mechanism: Each item creates a thread immediately. Nothing keeps the overlap at the cap of 2.

examples.summary: The queue accepts 8 jobs and reports a max size of 0, which means unbounded.
examples.mechanism: Queue() with no maxsize never refuses a put. The caller can keep enqueueing.
examples.expected_behavior: a positive max size, and no more jobs than that size

examples.summary: The holder keeps the lock while it waits, so the second acquire prints blocked.
examples.mechanism: The lock is acquired before the wait and released after it. The other thread cannot enter.

examples.summary: gather starts all 8 jobs and reports that all 8 finished.
examples.mechanism: The comprehension builds one coroutine per item and gather schedules every one of them.
